column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|11-16|2006|Μίλτον Φρίντμαν|Milton Friedman|Milton Friedman was an American economist. He led the Chicago School and supported free markets. In 1976 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics. He died in 2006.
bio|11-17|9|Βεσπασιανός|Vespasian|Vespasian was born in 9 AD. He was Roman emperor from 69 to 79 and the founder of the Flavian dynasty. He began the construction of the Colosseum.

bio|11-17|1558|Μαρία Α΄|Mary I|Mary I was queen of England from 1553 to 1558. She tried to restore Catholicism, and many Protestants were burned at the stake, which is why she was called "Bloody Mary". She died in 1558.

bio|11-17|1796|Αικατερίνη Β΄|Catherine the Great|Catherine II the Great was empress of Russia from 1762 to 1796. She was born in Germany. She expanded the empire towards the Black Sea and Poland and was a patron of the arts. She died in 1796.

bio|11-17|1887|Μπέρναρντ Μοντγκόμερι|Bernard Montgomery|Bernard Montgomery was a British field marshal. He defeated Rommel at the Battle of El Alamein in 1942 and commanded the British forces in Normandy. He died in 1976.

bio|11-17|1902|Γιουτζίν Γουίγκνερ|Eugene Wigner|Eugene Wigner was born in Budapest and lived in the United States. He was a physicist and mathematician. He applied group theory to quantum mechanics and in 1963 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1995.
bio|11-17|1917|Ωγκύστ Ροντέν|Auguste Rodin|Auguste Rodin died in 1917. He was a French sculptor and the creator of the works "The Thinker" and "The Kiss".
bio|11-17|1942|Μάρτιν Σκορσέζε|Martin Scorsese|Martin Scorsese is an American director. He directed the films "Taxi Driver", "Raging Bull", "Goodfellas" and "The Departed", for which he won an Oscar.

bio|11-17|1952|Σίριλ Ραμαφόζα|Cyril Ramaphosa|Cyril Ramaphosa is a South African politician and former trade unionist. He has been president of South Africa since 2018, as leader of the African National Congress.
bio|11-17|2013|Ντόρις Λέσινγκ|Doris Lessing|Doris Lessing died in 2013. She was a British writer and in 2007 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She wrote "The Golden Notebook".

bio|11-18|1786|Κάρλ Μαρία φον Βέμπερ|Carl Maria von Weber|Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer and pianist. He wrote the opera "Der Freischütz", which is regarded as the first great German Romantic opera. He died in 1826.
bio|11-18|1886|Τσέστερ Άρθουρ|Chester A. Arthur|Chester A. Arthur was the 21st president of the United States, from 1881 to 1885. He died in 1886.
bio|11-18|1897|Πάτρικ Μπλάκετ|Patrick Blackett|Patrick Blackett was an English physicist. He studied cosmic radiation and in 1948 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1974.
bio|11-18|1922|Μαρσέλ Προυστ|Marcel Proust|Marcel Proust died in 1922. He was a French writer and wrote the seven-volume "In Search of Lost Time".

bio|11-18|1939|Μάργκαρετ Άτγουντ|Margaret Atwood|Margaret Atwood is a Canadian writer. She wrote "The Handmaid's Tale" and "The Blind Assassin". She has won many awards, among them the Booker Prize twice.
bio|11-18|1940|Καμπούς μπιν Σαΐντ|Qaboos bin Said|Qaboos bin Said was sultan of Oman from 1970 until his death in 2020. He overthrew his father and modernised the country.
bio|11-18|1941|Βάλτερ Νερνστ|Walther Nernst|Walther Nernst died in 1941. He was a German physical chemist and in 1920 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his heat theorem.
bio|11-18|1962|Νιλς Μπορ|Niels Bohr|Niels Bohr died in 1962 in Copenhagen. He was a Danish physicist who developed the Bohr model of the atom, and in 1922 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.
bio|11-18|1968|Όουεν Γουίλσον|Owen Wilson|Owen Wilson is an American actor. He became known for comedies such as "Zoolander" and "Wedding Crashers". He also appeared in "Midnight in Paris".
bio|11-19|1600|Κάρολος Α΄|Charles I|Charles I was king of England from 1625. He came into conflict with Parliament and was defeated in the Civil War. He was tried and beheaded in 1649.

bio|11-19|1665|Νικολά Πουσέν|Nicolas Poussin|Nicolas Poussin was a French painter of Classicism. He lived in Rome and painted mythological and biblical subjects with strict composition. He died in 1665.
bio|11-19|1711|Μιχαήλ Λομονόσοφ|Mikhail Lomonosov|Mikhail Lomonosov was a Russian polymath. He became a physicist, chemist, astronomer and poet, and he founded Moscow University. He died in 1765.

bio|11-19|1828|Φραντς Σούμπερτ|Franz Schubert|Franz Schubert was an Austrian composer of Romanticism. He wrote more than 600 songs, with the cycle "Winter Journey", and symphonies such as the "Unfinished". He died young, in 1828, at the age of 31.
bio|11-19|1831|Τζέιμς Γκάρφιλντ|James Garfield|James Garfield was the 20th president of the United States. He was shot in July 1881 and died on 19 September, a few months after taking office.
bio|11-19|1917|Ίντιρα Γκάντι|Indira Gandhi|Indira Gandhi was an Indian politician. She was prime minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980. She was assassinated in 1984.
bio|11-19|1962|Τζόντι Φόστερ|Jodie Foster|Jodie Foster is an American actress and director. She won two Oscars, for "The Accused" and "The Silence of the Lambs".

bio|11-19|2013|Φρέντερικ Σάνγκερ|Frederick Sanger|Frederick Sanger died in 2013. He was an English biochemist who won two Nobel Prizes in Chemistry, one for the structure of insulin and one for the method of DNA sequencing.

bio|11-19|2017|Τσαρλς Μάνσον|Charles Manson|Charles Manson was an American criminal and the leader of a heretical group, the "Family". He was convicted for the murders of 1969 and died in prison in 2017.

bio|11-20|1858|Σέλμα Λάγκερλεφ|Selma Lagerlöf|Selma Lagerlöf was a Swedish writer. She wrote "The Wonderful Adventures of Nils" and in 1909 she became the first woman to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in 1940.

bio|11-20|1889|Έντουιν Χαμπλ|Edwin Hubble|Edwin Hubble was an American astronomer. He proved that there are galaxies beyond our own and that the universe is expanding. The Hubble Space Telescope bears his name. He died in 1953.
bio|11-20|1910|Λέων Τολστόι|Leo Tolstoy|Leo Tolstoy died in 1910 at Astapovo station. He was a Russian writer, with works such as "War and Peace" and "Anna Karenina".
bio|11-20|1923|Ναντίν Γκόρντιμερ|Nadine Gordimer|Nadine Gordimer was a South African writer and an activist against apartheid. In 1991 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in 2014.

bio|11-20|1925|Ρόμπερτ Κένεντι|Robert F. Kennedy|Robert Kennedy was an American politician and brother of President John F. Kennedy. He was Attorney General and a senator. He was assassinated in 1968 during his election campaign.

bio|11-20|1942|Τζο Μπάιντεν|Joe Biden|Joe Biden is an American Democratic politician. He was a senator for Delaware, vice president to Barack Obama and the 46th president of the United States, from 2021 to 2025.
bio|11-20|1952|Μπενεντέτο Κρότσε|Benedetto Croce|Benedetto Croce was an Italian philosopher and historian. He wrote about aesthetics and history and was an opponent of fascism. He died in 1952.
bio|11-20|1975|Φρανθίσκο Φράνκο|Francisco Franco|Francisco Franco was a Spanish general and dictator. He won the Spanish Civil War and governed Spain from 1939 until his death in 1975.
bio|11-20|2006|Ρόμπερτ Όλτμαν|Robert Altman|Robert Altman was an American director. He directed the films "M*A*S*H", "Nashville" and "The Player". He died in 2006.

bio|11-21|1694|Βολταίρος|Voltaire|Voltaire, whose real name was François-Marie Arouet, was a French philosopher and writer of the Enlightenment. He wrote "Candide" and supported tolerance and freedom of speech. He died in 1778.
bio|11-21|1695|Χένρι Πέρσελ|Henry Purcell|Henry Purcell died in 1695. He was an English Baroque composer, known for the opera "Dido and Aeneas".

bio|11-21|1811|Χάινριχ φον Κλάιστ|Heinrich von Kleist|Heinrich von Kleist was a German writer. He wrote "Michael Kohlhaas" and the play "The Prince of Homburg". He took his own life in 1811, at the age of 34.
bio|11-21|1898|Ρενέ Μαγκρίτ|René Magritte|René Magritte was a Belgian painter of Surrealism, known for the painting "This Is Not a Pipe". He died in 1967.

bio|11-21|1902|Ισαάκ Μπάσεβις Σίνγκερ|Isaac Bashevis Singer|Isaac Bashevis Singer was a Polish-Jewish writer who wrote in Yiddish and lived in the United States. In 1978 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1991.

bio|11-21|1916|Φραγκίσκος Ιωσήφ Α΄|Franz Joseph I|Franz Joseph I was emperor of Austria and king of Hungary from 1848. He reigned for 68 years and was emperor at the outbreak of the First World War. He died in 1916.
bio|11-21|1935|Φαϊρούζ|Fairuz|Fairuz is a Lebanese singer and one of the greatest voices of the Arab world. She became known with the Rahbani brothers and with songs about Lebanon.
bio|11-21|1965|Μπιορκ|Björk|Björk is an Icelandic singer and songwriter. She began with The Sugarcubes and as a solo artist she has made experimental pop, with albums such as "Homogenic".
bio|11-21|1970|Τσαντρασεκάρα Ράμαν|C. V. Raman|C. V. Raman died in 1970. He was an Indian physicist and in 1930 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for the Raman effect.
bio|11-22|1819|Τζορτζ Έλιοτ|George Eliot|George Eliot, whose real name was Mary Ann Evans, was an English writer. She wrote the novels "Middlemarch" and "The Mill on the Floss". She died in 1880.
bio|11-22|1869|Αντρέ Ζιντ|André Gide|André Gide was a French writer. He wrote "The Counterfeiters" and in 1947 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1951.

bio|11-22|1890|Σαρλ ντε Γκωλ|Charles de Gaulle|Charles de Gaulle was born in 1890 in Lille. He was a French general and politician, the leader of Free France and president of France from 1959 to 1969. He died in 1970.
bio|11-22|1916|Τζακ Λόντον|Jack London|Jack London died in 1916. He was an American journalist and writer of "White Fang" and "The Call of the Wild".

bio|11-22|1963|Τζον Φιτζέραλντ Κένεντι|John F. Kennedy|John F. Kennedy was the 35th president of the United States, from 1961. He was assassinated on 22 November 1963 in Dallas, Texas, at the age of 46.
bio|11-22|1963|Άλντους Χάξλεϋ|Aldous Huxley|Aldous Huxley died in 1963, on the same day as Kennedy. He was an English writer and wrote "Brave New World".

bio|11-22|1963|Κλάιβ Στέιπλς Λιούις|C. S. Lewis|C. S. Lewis was a British writer and professor. He wrote "The Chronicles of Narnia" and theological essays, such as "Mere Christianity". He died in 1963.
bio|11-22|1967|Μαρκ Ράφαλο|Mark Ruffalo|Mark Ruffalo is an American actor. He appeared in "Spotlight" and "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind" and plays the Hulk in Marvel films.
bio|11-22|1984|Σκάρλετ Τζοχάνσον|Scarlett Johansson|Scarlett Johansson is an American actress. She became known with "Lost in Translation" and as the Black Widow in Marvel films.
bio|10-15|1542|Ακμπάρ ο Μέγας|Akbar the Great|Akbar the Great was born in 1542. He was emperor of the Mughal Empire of India and promoted a policy of religious tolerance. He died in 1605.
bio|11-23|1572|Άνιολο Μπροντσίνο|Agnolo Bronzino|Agnolo Bronzino was an Italian painter of Mannerism from Florence. He painted portraits of the Medici court and allegorical works. He died in 1572.
bio|11-23|1804|Φράνκλιν Πιρς|Franklin Pierce|Franklin Pierce was the 14th president of the United States, from 1853 to 1857. He died in 1869.

bio|11-23|1887|Μπόρις Κάρλοφ|Boris Karloff|Boris Karloff was an English actor. He became famous for the role of the monster in the 1931 film "Frankenstein" and as an actor in horror films. He died in 1969.
bio|11-23|1962|Νικολάς Μαδούρο|Nicolás Maduro|Nicolás Maduro is a Venezuelan politician. He succeeded Hugo Chávez in 2013 and led Venezuela through a period of deep economic and political crisis.
bio|11-23|1976|Αντρέ Μαλρώ|André Malraux|André Malraux was a French writer and politician. He wrote "Man's Fate" and was Minister of Culture under de Gaulle. He died in 1976.
bio|11-23|1990|Ρόαλντ Νταλ|Roald Dahl|Roald Dahl died in 1990. He was a Welsh writer of children's books, such as "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory" and "Matilda".

bio|11-23|1992|Μάιλι Σάιρους|Miley Cyrus|Miley Cyrus is an American singer and actress. She became known for the children's series "Hannah Montana" and later as a singer, with hits such as "Wrecking Ball" and "Flowers".
bio|11-23|2006|Αλεξάντερ Λιτβινένκο|Alexander Litvinenko|Alexander Litvinenko was a former Russian spy and a critic of Vladimir Putin. He died in 2006 in London, from poisoning with polonium-210.

bio|11-24|1632|Μπαρούχ Σπινόζα|Baruch Spinoza|Baruch Spinoza was a Dutch philosopher of Portuguese-Jewish origin. He wrote "Ethics" and supported a pantheistic conception of God. He was excommunicated by the Jewish community. He died in 1677.
bio|11-24|1730|Αλεξάντερ Βασίλιεβιτς Σουβόροφ|Alexander Suvorov|Alexander Suvorov was a Russian general. He never lost a battle in his long career and crossed the Alps in 1799. He died in 1800.
bio|11-24|1784|Ζαχαρίας Τέιλορ|Zachary Taylor|Zachary Taylor was the 12th president of the United States and a general, a hero of the war with Mexico. He died in 1850, in office.
bio|11-24|1826|Κάρλο Κολόντι|Carlo Collodi|Carlo Collodi was an Italian writer. He wrote the book "The Adventures of Pinocchio" in 1883. He died in 1890.

bio|11-24|1864|Ανρί ντε Τουλούζ-Λωτρέκ|Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec|Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French painter and poster artist. He depicted the nightlife of Paris, with the Moulin Rouge. He died in 1901.
bio|11-24|1929|Ζωρζ Κλεμανσώ|Georges Clemenceau|Georges Clemenceau died in 1929. He was a French politician and prime minister at the end of the First World War, known as "the Tiger".

bio|11-24|1957|Ντιέγκο Ριβέρα|Diego Rivera|Diego Rivera was a Mexican painter. He created large murals on subjects from the history and society of Mexico and was married to Frida Kahlo. He died in 1957.

bio|11-24|1991|Φρέντι Μέρκιουρι|Freddie Mercury|Freddie Mercury died in 1991. He was the singer of Queen, with hits such as "Bohemian Rhapsody". He died of complications from AIDS, a day after announcing that he was ill.

bio|11-24|2002|Τζον Ρωλς|John Rawls|John Rawls was an American philosopher. He wrote "A Theory of Justice" in 1971, one of the most important works of political philosophy of the 20th century. He died in 2002.
bio|11-25|1562|Λόπε δε Βέγα|Lope de Vega|Lope de Vega was a Spanish playwright of the Golden Age. He wrote hundreds of plays, such as "Fuenteovejuna". He died in 1635.

bio|11-25|1844|Καρλ Μπεντς|Karl Benz|Karl Benz was a German engineer. In 1885 he built the first car with an internal combustion engine, and in 1886 he received the patent for the Benz Patent-Motorwagen. He died in 1929.

bio|11-25|1915|Αουγούστο Πινοσέτ|Augusto Pinochet|Augusto Pinochet was a Chilean general. He led the coup of 1973 and governed Chile as a dictator until 1990. Serious violations of human rights took place during his time. He died in 2006.

bio|11-25|1950|Γιοχάνες Βίλχελμ Γένσεν|Johannes Vilhelm Jensen|Johannes Vilhelm Jensen died in 1950. He was a Danish writer who wrote the epic "The Long Journey", and in 1944 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|11-25|1970|Γιούκιο Μισίμα|Yukio Mishima|Yukio Mishima was a Japanese writer, actor and director. He wrote "Confessions of a Mask" and "The Temple of the Golden Pavilion". He took his own life by seppuku in 1970, after a failed coup attempt.

bio|11-25|1971|Κριστίνα Άπλγκεϊτ|Christina Applegate|Christina Applegate is an American actress. She became known for the series "Married... with Children" and appeared in the films "Anchorman" and "Bad Moms".

bio|11-25|1981|Τσάμπι Αλόνσο|Xabi Alonso|Xabi Alonso is a former Spanish footballer and coach. He played as a midfielder for Liverpool, Real Madrid and Bayern, and won the World Cup in 2010 and the Euro 2008 and 2012.
bio|11-25|2016|Φιντέλ Κάστρο|Fidel Castro|Fidel Castro died in 2016. He was a Cuban revolutionary and the leader of Cuba from 1959, when he overthrew Batista, until 2008.

bio|11-25|2020|Ντιέγκο Μαραντόνα|Diego Maradona|Diego Maradona died on 25 November 2020, at the age of 60. He was an Argentine footballer and one of the greatest of all time, a winner of the 1986 World Cup.

bio|11-26|1504|Ισαβέλλα Α΄|Isabella I|Isabella I was queen of Castile from 1474. With her husband Ferdinand of Aragon she united the kingdoms of Spain, completed the Reconquista and financed Columbus's voyage. She died in 1504.

bio|11-26|1516|Τζοβάνι Μπελλίνι|Giovanni Bellini|Giovanni Bellini was an Italian painter from Venice. He was among the pioneers of Venetian painting and the teacher of Titian and Giorgione. He died in 1516.

bio|11-26|1855|Άνταμ Μιτσκιέβιτς|Adam Mickiewicz|Adam Mickiewicz was a Polish poet of Romanticism. He wrote the epic "Pan Tadeusz" and is regarded as Poland's national poet. He died in 1855 in Constantinople.
bio|11-26|1857|Φερντινάν ντε Σοσίρ|Ferdinand de Saussure|Ferdinand de Saussure was a Swiss linguist. His "Course in General Linguistics" founded structural linguistics and semiology. He died in 1913.
bio|11-26|1894|Νόρμπερτ Βίνερ|Norbert Wiener|Norbert Wiener was an American mathematician. He was the founder of cybernetics and wrote "Cybernetics". He died in 1964.
bio|11-26|1909|Ευγένιος Ιονέσκο|Eugène Ionesco|Eugène Ionesco was a Romanian-French playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd. He wrote "The Bald Soprano" and "Rhinoceros". He died in 1994.
bio|11-26|1939|Αμπντουλάχ Αχμέτ Μπαντάουι|Abdullah Ahmad Badawi|Abdullah Ahmad Badawi is a Malaysian politician. He was prime minister of Malaysia from 2003 to 2009.
bio|11-26|1981|Μαξ Όυβε|Max Euwe|Max Euwe was a Dutch chess player. He was world champion from 1935 to 1937 and later president of FIDE. He died in 1981.
bio|11-26|1990|Ρίτα Όρα|Rita Ora|Rita Ora was born in Pristina and is a British singer and actress. She became known with hits such as "Hot Right Now" and "Anywhere".

bio|11-27|511|Κλόβις Α΄|Clovis I|Clovis I was the founder of the Frankish kingdom and of the Merovingian dynasty. Through his baptism he brought the Franks into the Western Church, and he ruled from 481 to 511.
bio|11-27|1701|Άντερς Κέλσιος|Anders Celsius|Anders Celsius was a Swedish astronomer. He developed the Celsius temperature scale. He died young, in 1744.

bio|11-27|1852|Άντα Λάβλεϊς|Ada Lovelace|Ada Lovelace was an English mathematician and the daughter of the poet Lord Byron. She worked with Charles Babbage and wrote the first program for an analytical engine. She is regarded as one of the first programmers. She died in 1852.

bio|11-27|1921|Αλεξάντερ Ντούμπτσεκ|Alexander Dubček|Alexander Dubček was a Slovak politician. As leader of Czechoslovakia in 1968 he began the "Prague Spring", which was suppressed by the forces of the Warsaw Pact. He died in 1992.
bio|11-27|1940|Μπρους Λι|Bruce Lee|Bruce Lee was born in 1940 in San Francisco. He was an actor and a pioneer of martial arts, and he died in 1973.
bio|11-27|1942|Τζίμι Χέντριξ|Jimi Hendrix|Jimi Hendrix was an American guitarist and singer. He is regarded as one of the greatest rock guitarists. He died in 1970.
bio|11-27|1953|Ευγένιος Ο'Νηλ|Eugene O'Neill|Eugene O'Neill died in 1953. He was an American playwright and in 1936 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|11-27|1960|Γιούλια Τιμοσένκο|Yulia Tymoshenko|Yulia Tymoshenko is a Ukrainian politician. She was prime minister of Ukraine and a leading figure of the Orange Revolution in 2004.

bio|11-27|1985|Φερνάν Μπρωντέλ|Fernand Braudel|Fernand Braudel was a French historian. He led the "Annales" school and wrote "The Mediterranean and the Mediterranean World in the Age of Philip II". He died in 1985.

bio|11-28|1680|Τζαν Λορέντσο Μπερνίνι|Gian Lorenzo Bernini|Gian Lorenzo Bernini was an Italian sculptor and architect, the leading figure of Roman Baroque. He created "The Ecstasy of Saint Teresa" and the square of Saint Peter's. He died in 1680.

bio|11-28|1694|Ματσούο Μπασό|Matsuo Bashō|Matsuo Bashō was a Japanese poet and the most important master of haiku. His work "The Narrow Road to the Deep North" is a travel diary in haiku. He died in 1694.
bio|11-28|1757|Ουίλιαμ Μπλέικ|William Blake|William Blake was an English poet, painter and engraver. He wrote and illustrated "Songs of Innocence and of Experience". He died in 1827.
bio|11-28|1820|Φρίντριχ Ένγκελς|Friedrich Engels|Friedrich Engels was a German philosopher and businessman. He worked with Marx and wrote "The Communist Manifesto" with him. He died in 1895.
bio|11-28|1880|Αλεξάντρ Μπλοκ|Alexander Blok|Alexander Blok was a Russian poet of Symbolism. He wrote the poem "The Twelve". He died in 1921.

bio|11-28|1881|Στέφαν Τσβάιχ|Stefan Zweig|Stefan Zweig was an Austrian writer and journalist. He wrote "The World of Yesterday" and many short stories. He left Europe because of the Nazis and took his own life in 1942 in Brazil.

bio|11-28|1908|Κλοντ Λεβί-Στρος|Claude Lévi-Strauss|Claude Lévi-Strauss was a French anthropologist and the founder of structural anthropology. He wrote "Tristes Tropiques". He died in 2009, at the age of 100.
bio|11-28|1954|Ενρίκο Φέρμι|Enrico Fermi|Enrico Fermi died in 1954. He was an Italian physicist. He built the first nuclear reactor in 1942, and in 1938 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.
bio|11-28|1968|Ένιντ Μπλάιτον|Enid Blyton|Enid Blyton died in 1968. She was an English author of children's books. She wrote more than 700 books, with series such as "The Famous Five".

bio|11-29|1643|Κλαούντιο Μοντεβέρντι|Claudio Monteverdi|Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer. He wrote "Orfeo" in 1607, one of the first operas, and made the transition from the Renaissance to the Baroque. He died in 1643.
